headline: BARRICK ABX Q2 OUT AT 6AM: $5.1B REVENUE CONSENSUS AT FIRST FULL $4,300+ GOLD QUARTER — NEWCO SPIN-OFF CALL 11AM ET
source_name: Barrick Mining Corp (TSX: ABX / NYSE: B)
snippet: Barrick Mining Corporation (TSX: ABX; NYSE: B) released its second-quarter 2026 results at 6:00 AM ET this morning — the first major gold producer to report a full quarter with gold averaging approximately $4,300+ per ounce. Consensus analyst estimates ahead of the print were $5.1016 billion in consolidated revenue, $0.81 EPS, and quarterly gold production in the 730,000–770,000 ounce guidance range, with a consensus realized gold price of approximately $4,507/oz — roughly 37% above Q2 2025 levels. Barrick beat consensus EPS in three of its last four quarters with an average positive earnings surprise of 14.1%, and its Q1 2026 print (released May 11) established the benchmark: production of 719,000 oz (beating 640–680K guidance), revenue of $5.22 billion, attributable free cash flow of $1.21 billion up 195% year-on-year, and net earnings of $1.60 billion ($0.96/share). CEO Mark Bristow's 11:00 AM ET webcast is where retail investors should focus: the primary strategic question is a timeline update on the proposed NewCo spin-off — a planned NYSE/TSX IPO of Barrick's North American assets including its 61.5% interest in Nevada Gold Mines (the Carlin, Cortez, and Turquoise Ridge joint venture with Newmont) and Pueblo Viejo in the Dominican Republic, a structure that analysts have valued at approximately US$60 billion. At current gold prices and with the gold equity sector in breakout mode after GDX/GDXJ's best five-day performance of 2026, any concrete NewCo IPO timeline update on today's call would be a material catalyst — the complexity discount in Barrick's current multiple relative to sum-of-the-parts valuation is the most significant value unlock available to Barrick shareholders in the near term.

headline: HELIOSTAR HSTR Q2 RECORD: $56.5M REVENUE, 14,803 OZ GOLD, $43M CASH — TSXV JUNIOR PROVES THE BULL MARKET MATH
snippet: Heliostar Metals Ltd. (TSXV: HSTR; OTC: HSTXF) reported August 7, 2026 its strongest quarter in company history for Q2 2026: record gold production of 14,803 ounces and 79,710 ounces of silver, record revenues of $56.5 million, record mine operating earnings of $31.1 million, net income of $8.0 million ($0.03/share), and a record cash balance of $43.0 million with zero debt. All-in sustaining costs for Q2 were $2,287/oz gold sold — generating approximately $2,000+/oz in all-in margin against a realized gold price in the $4,200–$4,300 range. Gold production at the San Agustin mine increased 49% quarter-on-quarter, and the company is on track for full-year 2026 guidance of 50,000–55,000 gold ounces. A conference call for analysts and investors is scheduled for today, Monday August 10, at 1:00 PM ET. For retail investors looking for documented evidence that the current gold bull market is creating real free cash flow at TSXV-listed junior producers — rather than purely speculative exploration premiums — Heliostar's Q2 print is a clean data point: a no-debt, cash-accumulating gold producer at $43M cash balance and $0.03/share earnings, operating at cash costs of $1,654/oz against ~$4,300 gold. The bull market math is straightforward: at $1,654/oz cash cost and $4,300 spot, the margin has tripled from what it was at $2,600 gold two years ago. That operational leverage is now flowing through as reported earnings.

headline: FOUNDERS METALS FR249: 28.0m @ 14.27 g/t GOLD — HIGHEST-GRADE HOLE OUTSIDE FROYO CORE EXTENDS ANTINO DEPTH BY 50m
snippet: Founders Metals Inc. (CSE: FDR; OTCQB: FDMIF) announced August 6, 2026 the highest-grade drill hole reported to date outside the mapped high-grade Froyo core at its Antino Gold Project in southeastern Suriname: hole FR249 returned 28.0 metres grading 14.27 g/t gold from 433.0 metres downhole — approximately 340 metres vertical depth — as a 50-metre down-dip extension of a previously drilled section (FR175: 10.0m @ 5.90 g/t gold). FR249 also intersected three additional stacked mineralized intervals above the headline result: 18.0m @ 1.04 g/t gold from 285.0m, 24.0m @ 0.36 g/t gold from 319.0m, and 6.0m @ 1.62 g/t gold from 415.0m. The geological significance is material: 14.27 g/t over 28 metres at 340 metres vertical, confirmed well outside the previously mapped high-grade core, demonstrates that the Antino gold system extends at depth with grade continuity that supports potential underground mining scenarios above current planning assumptions. Additional holes in the August 6 release tested parallel shears across Upper Antino from 45m to 460m down-hole, returning results consistent with the multi-zone, stacked shear character of the system. Antino is one of the highest-grade undeveloped gold systems currently in active exploration in South America, and FR249 is the strongest signal to date that the deposit's grade profile extends meaningfully deeper than initially modelled — a key variable in any future resource estimate and mine plan.

headline: PERPETUA STIBNITE: 21.3m @ 3.2 g/t Au + 0.9% TUNGSTEN — FIRST DRILL IN A DECADE OPENS THIRD CRITICAL MINERAL AT CONSTRUCTION-STAGE IDAHO MINE
snippet: Perpetua Resources Corp (Nasdaq: PPTA) reported August 6, 2026 results from the first exploratory drilling in nearly a decade at its Stibnite Gold Project in central Idaho — a project already under active construction with a $2.9 billion Export-Import Bank loan, designed to supply approximately 35% of US antimony demand in its first six years of operation. The new drill results identify tungsten as a third critical mineral alongside gold and antimony: the Clark Tunnel Fault Zone returned 21.3 metres at 3.2 g/t gold with 0.9% tungsten, while Hangar Flats antimony-tungsten zones returned up to 22.9 metres at 3.2% antimony and 1.2% tungsten — suggesting tungsten is a recoverable co-product rather than a trace contaminant. Near-surface gold-antimony results include 6.4 metres at 16.2 g/t gold and 1.7% antimony, and 3.0 metres at 14.5 g/t gold at Hangar Flats. For US critical mineral investors, Stibnite's strategic profile has just expanded: the US currently has zero domestic tungsten primary production and imports approximately 70% from China, meaning a constructed Idaho mine delivering gold, antimony (zero US domestic production), and tungsten from the same ore body would be uniquely irreplaceable in US critical mineral supply chains. A 10,000-metre 2026 core program is underway with approximately 5,800 metres already drilled; the results are informing resource expansion planning concurrent with active mine construction.

headline: TUDOR GOLD TUD: NEW COPPER-GOLD PORPHYRY DISCOVERED AT TREATY CREEK — PSP ZONE HITS 82.9m @ 0.21% Cu BESIDE $18.75M-OZ GOLDSTORM
source_name: The Globe and Mail / Tudor Gold (TSXV: TUD)
snippet: Tudor Gold Corp. (TSXV: TUD; FSE: TUC) announced August 6, 2026 the discovery of a new copper-gold-silver-molybdenum porphyry system at the Perfectstorm Zone on its Treaty Creek property in British Columbia's Golden Triangle — the PSP Zone, located approximately one kilometre southwest of the flagship Goldstorm Deposit (18.75 million ounces gold equivalent). Highlight results from the first four PSP Zone holes: PS-26-15 returned 82.90 metres at 0.24 g/t gold, 2.11 g/t silver, 0.21% copper, and 50.76 ppm molybdenum; PS-26-18 returned 67.35 metres at 0.34 g/t gold, 1.89 g/t silver, and 0.27% copper — all within a potassic-altered diorite porphyry intrusive characteristic of large-scale copper-gold porphyry systems globally. Simultaneously, the PSE Zone (gold-silver epithermal trend) was confirmed in the same drill program. The strategic significance for Treaty Creek investors is that the property now hosts two distinct mineral systems — a copper-gold porphyry and a gold-silver epithermal — within one kilometre of a deposit already endowed with nearly 19 million ounces of gold equivalent. Major mining company corporate development teams evaluating Treaty Creek must now model the Goldstorm Deposit plus potential copper-gold porphyry and epithermal satellite systems — a materially different acquisition evaluation than a single-deposit asset. The BC Golden Triangle is one of the world's most productive gold discovery corridors, and district-scale copper-gold porphyry additions at known projects are among the most consequential geological events an explorer can announce.

headline: AZTEC AZT.V TOMBSTONE ARIZONA: 88.4m @ 1.69 g/t AuEq IN OXIDE — NORTH EXTENSION ZONE OPENS AHEAD OF Q4/26 MAIDEN RESOURCE
snippet: Aztec Minerals Corp. (TSXV: AZT; OTC: AZZTF) announced in early August 2026 results from nine reverse-circulation holes at its Tombstone gold-silver project in southeastern Arizona, including the first step-out drilling into the recently acquired North Extension Zone — land Aztec purchased specifically to test the system's northward continuity. Highlight hole TR26-39 intersected 88.4 metres at 1.42 g/t gold and 14.58 g/t silver (1.69 g/t AuEq) from 10.7 metres, including a 6.1-metre high-grade core at 12.23 g/t gold and 56.28 g/t silver (13.25 g/t AuEq). Hole TR26-38 returned 97.5 metres at 1.06 g/t gold and 16.08 g/t silver from surface. Both holes confirm that the near-surface oxide gold-silver system extends north from the main deposit into the newly acquired land. Aztec holds an 85% interest in the Tombstone property within the historic Tombstone silver district of Arizona; the property is now 90 reverse-circulation holes deep into its 2025–2026 drill program with 11 additional North Extension step-out holes pending assay. A Q4 2026 maiden mineral resource estimate is targeted — the first formal resource for the historic Tombstone district in decades. The oxide mineralogy is the key economics point: heap-leach gold-silver recovery from oxide ore requires substantially lower capital investment than milling, making Tombstone a potential early-stage producer candidate at current gold prices rather than a multi-decade development project.

headline: SILVER AT $65 ON PAYROLLS DISASTER — AU:AG RATIO COMPRESSES TO 66x AS SIL SILVER MINERS ETF CLEARS 4-MONTH CEILING
snippet: Silver surged to $65.05 per ounce on August 7, 2026 — its highest level in seven weeks — driven by the July nonfarm payrolls report showing the US economy shed 23,000 jobs (consensus: +180,000), the fourth consecutive monthly payrolls miss and the largest absolute miss of 2026. Silver's August 7 advance materially outpaced gold's on a percentage basis — a classic ratio compression signal that historically precedes the most powerful legs of precious metals bull markets. The gold-silver ratio compressed from above 70x (its level through much of Q1 2026, when gold dominated the rally) toward approximately 66x — still elevated relative to the 50–60x range historically associated with mature precious metals bull markets, but moving in the structurally correct direction. The VanEck Silver Miners ETF (SIL) cleared the $43 technical ceiling that had capped the sector for four consecutive months — a breakout that silver investors and technical analysts had been watching as a confirming signal. Silver's unique demand structure — monetary metal driven by safe-haven and inflation flows, plus industrial metal driven by photovoltaic solar panel manufacturing (>100 million ounces per year and growing) and electrical contacts in EV systems — means it benefits from both the macro rate-cut environment supporting gold and the real-economy demand from the electrification build-out. As of August 9, silver was trading at $64.31/oz, holding above the $64 level established during the week's breakout.

headline: AYA GOLD TSX AYA ACQUIRES 259KM² MOROCCO EXPLORATION PACKAGE — ADDS 35% TO LAND POSITION AROUND ZGOUNDER SILVER MINE
snippet: Aya Gold & Silver Inc. (TSX: AYA) announced August 6, 2026 the acquisition of three mining licences and 18 exploration permits covering approximately 259 square kilometres across three distinct project areas in Morocco — the Zagora, Agadir-Melloul, and Goulmim projects — for consideration of MAD 10 million (approximately C$1.5 million) in cash and assumed debt. The acquisition increases Aya's total Moroccan land package from 732 km² to more than 991 km², a 35.4% expansion. The Zagora project (158.6 km², 11 permits) is the largest and is prospective for nickel-cobalt-lead-zinc-silver-gold mineralization in Ordovician sedimentary rocks 40 km south of the Bou-Azzer inlier — a geological district with established base and precious metal mineralization. An 18–24 month greenfield exploration programme is planned including geochemistry, hyperspectral studies, and mapping before drilling decisions. For retail investors evaluating Aya as an exploration growth story layered on its Zgounder silver operations — the largest producing silver mine in Morocco and North Africa — this acquisition is the second significant land expansion of 2026 and signals a systematic approach to building a multi-project Moroccan portfolio while operating cash flow from Zgounder funds greenfield exploration. At approximately C$1.5 million for 259 km² in a proven silver-base metals jurisdiction, the per-square-kilometre acquisition cost reflects early-stage exploration-stage pricing — an asymmetric opportunity structure if any of the new project areas shows drill-ready targets.

headline: FRONEMAN TARGETS URANIUM FROM SEAWATER AFTER 13 YEARS AT SIBANYE — OCEAN RESERVES 1,000x TERRESTRIAL; COMMERCIAL HURDLES REMAIN
snippet: Neal Froneman, who led Sibanye-Stillwater as CEO for 13 years and transformed it from a South African gold producer into a global precious and battery metals company with approximately 84,000 employees, announced August 7, 2026 plans to launch a new mining venture targeting uranium extraction from seawater. The theoretical resource base — approximately 4.5 billion tonnes of dissolved uranium in the world's oceans — is roughly 1,000 times the estimated total economic uranium in conventional terrestrial ore deposits. Commercial seawater uranium extraction relies on polymer adsorption technology that selectively binds dissolved uranyl ions from seawater; the technology has been demonstrated at small scale through US and Japanese research programmes, with the primary barriers to commercialisation being adsorption efficiency (amount of uranium recoverable per unit of polymer per cycle) and polymer durability over thousands of adsorption-desorption cycles. Froneman's entry as a credentialed mine builder, rather than a researcher, signals institutional capital beginning to evaluate seawater extraction as a long-duration hedge against terrestrial supply constraints — the same structural supply thesis that has driven spot uranium from under $50/lb to $86.50/lb (+20% year-on-year) as AI data centres accelerate nuclear demand through signed long-term power purchase agreements from Microsoft and Meta. For conventional uranium equity investors, the MiningMX report is primarily a sentiment data point: when one of the mining industry's most successful practitioners targets uranium's supply side with a technology-focused venture, it reflects the durability of the structural bull market thesis, while actual commercial seawater extraction remains a decades-long development horizon.

headline: SILVER OUTLOOK AUGUST 2026: ANALYSTS TARGET $70-$80 AS RATIO COMPRESSION TOWARDS GOLD ACCELERATES
snippet: Canadian Mining Report's August 2026 silver price outlook surveyed precious metals analysts following silver's breakout week that saw the metal rally from approximately $58 to $65 on the July nonfarm payrolls miss — the same macro catalyst that drove gold above $4,300 and triggered GDX/GDXJ's best five-day advance of 2026. The bullish consensus clusters around $70–$80 per ounce by year-end 2026, based on three converging drivers: monetary demand proportional to gold's structural strength at $4,300+ (driven by de-dollarisation, central bank diversification, and Asian household wealth reallocation); industrial demand from the global electrification build-out, where silver's photovoltaic applications consume over 100 million ounces annually and AI data centre power infrastructure adds incremental demand through high-efficiency electrical connections; and gold-silver ratio mean reversion from the current 66x toward the historically 'normal' 50–60x range. At $4,300 gold and a 55x ratio, silver prices to $78.18; at a 50x ratio, $86.00. The bearish counterargument centres on US recession risk: if the labour market data (July payrolls at -23,000) signals a genuine economic contraction, industrial silver demand from manufacturing would decline, potentially offsetting monetary demand. The analytical observation most relevant for junior mining investors: silver's historical tendency to lag gold early in a bull market and then dramatically outperform as the bull matures — the ratio compression from 70x toward 50–60x — is precisely what appears to be beginning now. SIL (silver miners ETF) clearing its $43 technical ceiling while the gold-silver ratio is compressing is the confirming indicator that retail capital is paying attention to.
